tokenizer.name: cl100k_base
tokenizer.implementation: lumen_core::tokenizer::count_tokens, the function the meter uses
tokenizer.caveat: cl100k_base is not Claude's tokenizer. Counts compare modes with one another; they are not a bill and not the number of tokens Claude would charge.
tokenizer.counted: the reply text of a tool call. The JSON-RPC envelope and `_meta` are not counted, exactly as the meter does not count them.
tokenizer.line_endings: files are read byte for byte from the git object database; no line-ending conversion happens anywhere

latency.clock: std::time::Instant, a monotonic clock, nanosecond resolution
latency.warmup_note: per series per pass, run the same way as the recorded runs, so caches, page tables and the ledger file are warm; hook spawns are warm-start, not first launch after boot
latency.percentile_method: nearest-rank: the percentile p of n runs is the run at rank ceil(p x n / 100) of the sorted runs, fastest first, with no interpolation. With n = 200 the median is run 100 (of the two middle runs of an even count, the faster), p90 is run 180, and p99 is run 198, which leaves the slowest 2 runs above it.
latency.samples_note: not written. Each series carries `pass_medians_ns`, the median of each pass on its own, in pass order: how far they sit from one another is how much the machine moved while the run was going on.

savings.reason: A saving's dollar value is priced at the model of the turn that read the call's result, over the rounds that followed it, and less the extra round the call cost: the savings engine derives these from a ledger's turns. A corpus run has no turns, so this document gives tokens only.
savings.calibration_note: Token figures are Claude's tokens, estimated from the cl100k_base counts Lumen records (OpenAI's tokenizer: Claude's is not available offline), by the calibration of 2026-10-14, measured through Claude Code 2.1.296 against Claude's own usage data on 60 samples of raw file text. Each count is converted by its file's type and the model of the turn that read it, at the median ratio for them, with the smallest to the largest ratio any sample came out at as its band (not the 10th to 90th percentile: the floor is the band's low end, and must hold call by call); a row with no measured model takes the type's ratio over both tokenizers, weighted alike, with a band that spans them. The ratios are of raw file text: an answer Lumen makes from a file (an outline, a slice, a stub), a Read's line numbers and the tool-result wrapper around any answer, a Read's or Lumen's, are in no row. So an answer Lumen made takes the file's median, with the smallest to the largest ratio of any sample the model was sent as its band (of any sample at all where the model is not known). The dollar floor takes the low end of each saving: the file at its smallest ratio less Lumen's answer at its largest.
